articles.title: Football Daily - Premier League confirm Man City guilty of all charges - 5 Live Reaction - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Kelly Somers is joined by Dale Johnson, Kieran Maguire, John Murray and Paul Robinson
articles.body:
Radio 5 Live , · 29 Sep 2026 , · 34 mins

Kelly Somers gets the latest on the huge breaking news story, that the Premier League confirmed that Manchester City have been found guilty of all charges related to breaches of Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18. Kelly breaks down a really damning statement from the Premier League and with her to do that is the BBC’s football issues correspondent Dale Johnson, football finance expert Kieran Maguire from the Price of Football podcast, as well as football correspondent John Murray and former England goalkeeper Paul Robinson. They also hear from former Manchester City chairman David Bernstein – who said the Premier League statement was “damning beyond belief” and also get a fans perspective. Manchester City also released their own statement today saying the club are “both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League Commission” - they have until Friday to appeal.

articles.title: FIFA hits back at UEFA: Infantino's lawyers accuse European body of 'harassment'
articles.summary: FIFA lawyers have accused UEFA of harassing president Gianni Infantino and urged a Florida judge to reject the European soccer body's request for evidence
articles.body: FIFA lawyers have accused UEFA of harassing president Gianni Infantino and urged a Florida judge to reject the European soccer body's request for evidence related to a proposed private investment plan involving the 2026 World Cup, news agency Assocuated Press reported.In a 21-page filing submitted late Monday (local time) to the US District Court for the Southern District of Florida, FIFA lawyers said UEFA was wrong to suggest that Infantino sought to personally profit from the project, which caused a backlash in July before being dropped within days.UEFA has since asked three courts, including courts in Manhattan and Miami, to authorize discovery as it seeks information to help prepare a possible criminal complaint against Infantino in Switzerland over alleged financial mismanagement. One of the requests targets Josh Kushner's New York-based investment firm, while another relates to FIFA's office base in Miami.“UEFA’s conduct demonstrates that its (court filing) was made in bad faith and for the purpose of harassment,” FIFA lawyers said in the filing.The filing also pointed to the Nov. 18 deadline for candidates to enter the FIFA presidential election, which will be held in March in Morocco. Infantino is seeking a fourth and final term that would keep him in office through 2031.“This court should reject any attempt to influence FIFA’s presidential election based on these grounds,” FIFA lawyers wrote.What is the FIFA Forward Enterprise plan?UEFA led the backlash against the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan, which was proposed by Infantino. The plan involved creating a new FIFA subsidiary and selling at least 20% of FIFA's future commercial rights for $4.2 billion to a group of investors led by Josh Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.UEFA said in court filings last month that the proposed valuation was a “fraudulently off-market price promoted by Infantino for his own benefit.” The claim came amid speculation that Infantino could take a CEO-like role at the new subsidiary with a salary higher than his current $6 million presidential pay package.FIFA lawyers rejected that suggestion, saying UEFA “falsely asserts that Mr. Infantino sought to have a personal financial interest in the FFE project.”The plan was first reported by the media on July 28. It led to criticism from FIFA's then-chief operating officer Kevin Lamour, who was later removed from his position. Infantino's senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro, a former Goldman Sachs partner, also resigned in protest, saying the deal was bad for soccer.Infantino later apologised for errors in the way the plan was handled and offered to open an independent external review of FIFA's governance.FIFA has maintained that the proposed commercial spinoff was intended to accelerate the development of soccer around the world, particularly outside Europe's wealthier football markets.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Inspiring story of the day: “My father knew my head was in the clouds, so he made sure my feet were on the ground” - How Kylian Mbappé turned his parents’ unbreakable steel into football immortality
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappé’s rise from Bondy to Real Madrid and the France national team is closely tied to the lessons he learned at home and on the local pitches.
articles.body: Kylian Mbappé’s rise from Bondy to Real Madrid and the France national team is closely tied to the lessons he learned at home and on the local pitches. Before becoming a World Cup winner and one of football’s biggest stars, Mbappé spent his childhood playing for AS Bondy, where his father, Wilfried Mbappé, coached him and kept his ambitions under control. His mother, Fayza Lamari, also played a major role in protecting him as his fame grew. Mbappé has often spoken about how Bondy, his family and football shaped the person he became.How did Wilfried Mbappé keep Kylian Mbappé grounded in BondyFor Kylian Mbappé, Bondy was never simply the place where he started playing football. It was where he learned how to treat people, how to handle success and why his background mattered.In his 2020 article for The Players’ Tribune, Mbappé described a simple rule he learned while growing up. If 15 people were standing together and he knew only one of them, he was expected to greet everyone rather than just the person he knew.He explained:“There is actually a rule in Bondy that everyone understands. You learn it when you’re young. If you walk down the street and see 15 people standing on the corner, and you know only one of them, you have a choice. You either wave and walk on, or you go over and shake all 15 hands.”For Mbappé, that small habit represented something bigger. He said people in Bondy learned to treat everyone equally because they shared the same community.His football development followed a similar path. Mbappé trained at Clairefontaine during the week after being selected for the French national academy, but he still returned to Bondy at weekends to play for the team coached by his father.That meant he did not get to live only as a highly rated academy player. He still had to play in the environment where his father expected him to work for the team.Mbappé recalled one match when he tried a move based on what he had been learning at Clairefontaine. The decision went wrong, the opposition launched a counterattack and his father was furious.Wilfried told him:“Kylian! You are not here to try your fancy Clairefontaine experiences! We have a league to play here! You can go back to Clairefontaine all week and train on your nice field! But this is Bondy! Here, we have a life!!!”Mbappé later explained why that moment stayed with him:“I still carry that lesson with me everywhere I go. My father knew that my head was in the clouds, so he made sure that my feet were still on the ground.”What did Kylian Mbappé learn from Bondy before becoming a World Cup starMbappé’s childhood was not built around the expectation that he would become a global football star. In The Players’ Tribune, he wrote that he and his friends dreamed about football rather than expecting professional careers.That difference mattered to him.He remembered Bondy as a place where football was part of everyday life. The local pitches, school tournaments and games with friends gave him an environment away from the pressure that later followed him everywhere.His family also tried to protect that normal childhood. Even after Clairefontaine entered the picture, his parents wanted him to spend time at home rather than immediately moving into the world of a major football academy.Mbappé said his parents wanted him “to be a child and live a normal life”. Looking back, he felt those experiences taught him lessons that he might not have learned inside an academy bubble.That background became part of his identity when he reached the 2018 World Cup with France.Mbappé was only 19 when France won the tournament in Russia. Before France’s opening game against Australia, he shared a moment with Ousmane Dembélé in the tunnel.Mbappé recalled saying:“Look at us. The boy from Évreux. And the boy from Bondy. We are playing at the World Cup.”The memory showed how unusual the moment felt to him. He had gone from local football in Bondy to representing France on football’s biggest stage.At the end of his The Players’ Tribune letter, Mbappé returned to the children growing up in the suburbs and wrote:“We are the crazy dreamers. And lucky for us, dreaming doesn’t cost very much.”How did Fayza Lamari protect Kylian Mbappé as his fame grewWilfried Mbappé’s influence was strongly linked to football and discipline, while Fayza Lamari became an important figure as her son’s profile grew.Lamari, a former elite handball player, has also spoken publicly about how difficult Mbappé’s sudden fame became for the family. In an appearance on Demain le Sport, she described the effect of the constant attention around her son during his Paris Saint-Germain years.She said:“Kylian in Paris was like a magnifying glass on his flaws; he was no longer human. I had some very low moments. He can’t even walk down the street anymore. It makes me sad.”Lamari also said:“We are not prepared to become public figures.”Her comments gave a different view of Mbappé’s rise. The footballer was becoming one of the most recognisable athletes in the world, but his family was also dealing with the loss of privacy that came with that status. Goal reported Lamari’s comments from her appearance on Demain le Sport in October 2025.That family role continued as Mbappé built his life away from Bondy. His parents have remained involved in his wider projects, including Inspired by KM, the association created to support young people.Why does Inspired by KM matter to Kylian Mbappé’s Bondy storyMbappé’s connection to young people is not only something he talks about. In 2020, he launched Inspired by KM, an association built around helping 98 children work towards their own goals.According to Mbappé’s official website, the programme began with 49 boys and 49 girls aged between nine and 16. The project focuses on four values: learning, understanding, sharing and passing on what they learn.The organisation’s official website lists Kylian Mbappé as president and Fayza Lamari as treasurer. Its activities include language classes, cultural and sports trips, master classes and stays, with the children receiving individual support.Mbappé has also given money earned from his France career to charity. After the 2018 World Cup, his bonus was donated to Premiers de Cordée, an organisation that provides sports activities for hospitalised and disabled children. TF1 Info reported that the amount donated was around €400,000.That part of his story connects directly with what he learned in Bondy. His journey moved from a local artificial pitch to Clairefontaine, then Monaco, Paris Saint-Germain, the France national team and Real Madrid. But the lessons he has spoken about most clearly came from much earlier.His father taught him that talent could not excuse poor decisions. His mother saw first-hand what fame could take away from a family. And Bondy gave him a community where football was important, but respect mattered just as much.For Mbappé, that is where the story really began.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Oficial: La Premier declara culpable al City "de todos los cargos"
articles.standfirst: Duro comunicado en el que se relatan las tropelías del equipo de Manchester
articles.summary: Duro comunicado en el que se relatan las tropelías del equipo de Manchester
articles.body: La omisión independiente nombrada por la Premier League para investigar los movimientos financieros del Manchester City, ha declarado culpable al club de todos los cargos (115) relacionados con infracciones graves de las normas financieras de la Premier League durante un período de nueve temporadas, y de la mayoría de los cargos relacionados con su falta de cooperación con la investigación de la Liga. La Comisión independiente, compuesta por varios expertos legales, financieros y de otras áreas, ha declarado en un comunicado exhaustivo y durísimo, la lista de tropelías cometidas por el club: - El Manchester City organizó contratos ficticios (que tergiversaban el verdadero acuerdo entre las partes) con varios de sus socios comerciales, además de recurrir a acuerdos ficticios con otros, para inflar artificialmente los ingresos del club y reducir sus costos. - El club presentó cuentas falsas y ocultó el verdadero estado de sus finanzas a sus auditores y reguladores del fútbol . - El Manchester City incumplió significativamente los límites de gasto tanto de la Premier League como de la UEFA. - Durante la investigación de la Premier League, el Manchester City cometió múltiples incumplimientos de sus deberes de cooperación y de máxima buena fe hacia la Liga (tres de los cuatro presuntos incumplimientos fueron confirmados). La Comisión independiente determinó que el Manchester City realizó acuerdos comerciales ficticios con varios de sus patrocinadores durante ese período, como parte de un esquema de financiación encubierto, mediante el cual dichas empresas solo debían pagar una parte de las tarifas de patrocinio correspondientes. El resto fue financiado por Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd (ADUG), propietaria del club. Como parte de este esquema, se formalizaron otros acuerdos ficticios, financiados por ADUG, para que el club pudiera registrar gastos operativos inferiores a los reales, así como un acuerdo circular ficticio con Fordham, una entidad que adquirió los derechos de imagen de los jugadores del club, financiado también por ADUG. Se determinó que el propósito de estos planes era inflar artificialmente los ingresos del club y reducir sus costos en más de 900 millones de libras esterlinas durante el período afectado, para aparentar cumplir con las normas financieras. Como consecuencia, según constató la Comisión, el club presentó cuentas falsas y ocultó la verdadera situación financiera a sus auditores y a los organismos reguladores del fútbol. La Comisión concluyó que, "con su conducta, el club tenía la clara intención de eludir las normas de la Premier League". En consecuencia, el City no declaró con precisión sus ingresos y gastos a efectos del Reglamento de Rentabilidad y Sostenibilidad de la Premier League y del Reglamento de Licencias de Clubes y Juego Limpio Financiero de la UEFA. La Comisión determinó que, de haberse declarado con exactitud todos los acuerdos pertinentes en las cuentas del club, este habría incumplido los límites de gasto tanto de la Liga como de la UEFA por una cantidad muy considerable. Además, durante los cuatro años que duró la investigación llevada a cabo por la Premier League, el club incumplió en repetidas ocasiones sus deberes de cooperación y buena fe hacia la Liga. La Comisión concluyó que el club había realizado esfuerzos concertados para detener y obstaculizar la investigación de la Premier League. Ahora que se han probado los cargos, la cuestión de la sanción se abordará por separado en una audiencia posterior ante la Comisión independiente. De acuerdo con las normas de la Premier League, dicha audiencia se mantendrá privada y confidencial hasta que se permita la publicación del resultado. El club tiene derecho a apelar las conclusiones de la Comisión independiente y dispone de hasta el viernes 2 de octubre para ejercer ese derecho. La intención de la Junta Directiva de la Premier League es que todo el proceso (incluidas las apelaciones y la publicación de las decisiones pertinentes) concluya lo antes posible.

articles.title: Oregon's Dante Moore Vows to 'Be Back Soon' in Injury Update After Concussion vs. USC
articles.summary: Oregon quarterback Dante Moore has made his first public comment after suffering a concussion during Saturday's win over USC.
articles.body:
Oregon quarterback Dante Moore has made his first public comment after suffering a concussion during Saturday's win over USC.

In a post on Instagram, Moore thanked everyone for their support before saying he has "made progress" and vowed to "be back soon."

Moore was injured when he took a hard hit to the head and neck area by USC linebacker Desman Stephens II on a scramble in the second quarter.

Medical personnel took Moore off the field on a stretcher and he was taken in an ambulance to a local hospital for evaluation.

Oregon announced on Sunday that Moore's MRI and CT scans came back clean. He was officially diagnosed with a concussion but did not suffer any additional injuries.

There was no official timetable given for Moore's recovery, as the school explained they "are going to move forward with an abundance of caution" given the nature of concussions.

The hit from Stephens on Moore led to a scuffle involving players from both teams, but the officials and coaches from both schools were able to calm things down before it escalated.

Stephens, who issued an apology for the hit, was suspended by USC for its upcoming game against Washington.

Moore was off to a fantastic start in the game prior to the injury. He went 8-of-10 for 77 yards in three drives. The senior quarterback has thrown for 926 yards, seven touchdowns with a 69.7 completion percentage in four games.

Oregon has a bye this week before hosting UCLA on Oct. 10.

articles.title: Vicente Boluda también suma en la cantera del Levante
articles.standfirst: El empresario valenciano, a través de Boluda Corporación Marítima, se convierte en el principal patrocinador del fútbol base granota
articles.summary: El empresario valenciano, a través de Boluda Corporación Marítima, se convierte en el principal patrocinador del fútbol base granota
articles.body: Boluda Corporación Marítima es desde hoy el patrocinador principal de la cantera del Levante. El presidente de la compañía, accionista minoritario del conjunto valenciano y ex máximo mandatario del Real Madrid, Vicente Boluda, ha presentado junto al consejero delegado de la entidad granota, José Danvila, esta colaboración en el Ciutat de Valencia. Una cooperación que no solo busca reforzar la estructura del fútbol base, si no también, consolidar la apuesta por el desarrollo de la sociedad valenciana, el fomento de la actividad física y la formación integral de los jóvenes deportistas. "Para nosotros apoyar al Levante ha sido siempre la consigna. Empezando por mi abuelo, mi padre y yo personalmente, porque la historia del Levante ha estado siempre unida a la historia de Boluda Coporación Marítima porque los dos viven del mar y fundamentalmente de los poblados marítimos. Estamos encantados de apoyar al futuro del club", apunta Vicente Boluda. La figura del empresario valenciano ha estado ligada al club valenciano en diversas ocasiones y más concretamente desde el verano de 2023, donde estuvo muy cerca de entrar en la dirección junto al propio Danvila, y así mismo, como uno de los accionistas minoritarios más potentes tras la adquisición, este pasado mes de abril, de 4.130 acciones por un valor de 250.000 euros. Por su parte, José Danvila ha querido agradecer la confianza de la compañía y ha destacado que contar con el respaldo de una empresa referente a nivel internacional y profundamente vinculada al territorio valenciano “supone un impulso decisivo para seguir potenciando la cantera como uno de los pilares estratégicos y de identidad del club”. Mediante este acuerdo, la marca Boluda Corporación Marítima está presente de forma principal en el frontal de las camisetas de juego de los diferentes equipos masculinos y femeninos que integran la estructura de formación granota durante el curso 2026/2027.

articles.title: Premier League outlines Manchester City’s alleged breach of rules and ‘sham’ dealings
articles.summary: The Premier League has found Manchester City guilty of all of the charges related to serious breaches of the league’s financial rules.
articles.body: The Premier League has found Manchester City guilty of all of the charges related to serious breaches of the league’s financial rules. Sanctions related to the allegations have not been disclosed, though potential punishments against the club could include a points deduction, an unlimited fine, or even expulsion from the league entirely, according to the Premier League’s handbook. Manchester City has consistently denied any wrongdoing and in a statement released Tuesday, said it would “pursue the appeal avenues” following the Premier League’s disclosure and is “innocent of the accusations.” Within the Premier League’s statement, it said the independent commission found the Manchester, England-based club “arranged ‘sham’ contracts (which misrepresented the true agreement between the parties) with a number of its commercial partners, as well as relying on ‘sham’ agreements with others, to artificially inflate the club’s revenues and reduce its costs.” The Premier League posted the commission’s 40-page document, with multiple sentences and graphs redacted, outlining Man City’s alleged business schemes to circumvent the financial rules between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons. The case lays out “strong, cogent evidence” outlining “serious wrongdoing.” The case against the club states City “concealed the true state of its finances” and overstated “income across those years was consequently hugely overstated by over £830 million,” which converts to more than $1 billion. The club was also accused of understating its expenses by tens of millions of dollars. “The purpose of these schemes was found to have been to artificially inflate the club’s revenues, and reduce its costs, by more than £900 million during the affected period, to appear to comply with financial rules,” Tuesday’s Premier League statement decries. “The consequence of this, as the Commission found, was that the club filed misstated accounts and concealed the true state of its finances from its auditors and football regulators.” The league said the club failed to cooperate with the investigation – accusing the soccer powerhouse of committing “multiple breaches of its duties of co-operation and utmost good faith towards the League.” City’s CEO Ferran Soriano was defiant in an internal video message shared with staff and obtained by CNN, saying the club stands behind “irrefutable evidence” of its innocence and that accusations are based on “a single false accusation” and a “Premier League conspiracy theory.” Premier League chief executive Richard Masters said the commission’s decision vindicates the organization’s pursuit of the alleged hundreds of rule violations. “This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history,” Masters stated. “There are elements of the case that remain to be decided, including, importantly, what sanction must follow for these breaches.” An outcome years in the making While Premier League action has continued as normal on the pitch, the hearing and its potential findings have been bubbling away under the surface since the charges were announced in 2023. The club was charged in February of that year after a four-plus year investigation. On Tuesday, the Independent Commission noted it held a 42-day hearing that ended in December 2024 and that it regretted how long it took to publicly release the evidence. The league also accused City of failing to comply with UEFA’s financial fair play (FFP) regulations between 2013-14 and 2017-18 and failing to follow Premier League rules on profit and sustainability between 2015-16 and 2017-18. Manchester City won a total of eight trophies in the period covered by the case. This included three Premier League titles, three League Cups and one FA Cup. The 2010-11 FA Cup was City’s first major trophy in 35 years – their previous title coming in 1976. The 2011-12 Premier League title was the first of eight they have won to date. The hearing eventually started in September 2024 and carried on until the end of that year. At the time, former City manager Pep Guardiola said he was looking forward to having the matter settled. “I am happy that it starts on Monday,” Guardiola said in a press conference. “I know there will be more rumors and new specialists about the sentences will come up. We are going to see. I know what people are looking for, I know what they are expecting.” Guardiola continued: “Everybody is innocent until guilt is proven. An independent panel will decide, and I’m looking forward to the decision.” This was also not the first time that Manchester City had faced allegations over financial misconduct. In 2020, the club was initially banned from European soccer for two seasons for “serious breaches” of FFP regulations. The ban was later overturned by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), which also reduced the accompanying $34 million fine to $11.3 million, ruling that City had failed to cooperate with UEFA. Thomas Schlachter, Patrick Sung Cuadrado, Aleks Klosok, Jacob Lev and Kevin Dotson contributed to this report. This story has been updated with additional information.

articles.title: Asencio, más cerca del quirófano
articles.standfirst: El central sigue limitado por las molestias que sufre en la tibia desde hace nueve meses y la decisión de que se opere puede tomarse en breve
articles.summary: El central vuelve a parar por las molestias que sufre en la tibia desde hace nueve meses y la decisión de que se opere puede tomarse en breve
articles.body: Asencio está a un paso de tener que pasar por el quirófano para solucionar la lesión en la tibia de la pierna derecha que arrastra desde principios de año. MARCA ya adelantó a finales de agosto de esta posibilidad y la decisión está cada vez más cerca. Las molestias no remiten y un nuevo episodio de dolor en la zona dañada puede ser el detonante definitivo para que se tome la decisión de que sea intervenido quirúrgicamente. La operación lleva rondando a Asencio desde el final de la temporada pasada, cuando ya estuvo sobre la mesa esa opción, aprovechando el verano para amortiguar el largo tiempo de recuperación. Una baja que rondaría los 2-3 meses, lo que en el caso de confirmarse la operación llevaría al jugador a estar fuera de combate hasta principios de año, aproximadamente. Asencio se enfrentaba en este parón de tres semanas a un último intento para superar la lesión y evitar así el quirófano. Lo hacía, incluso, con la motivación de tener el premio de la titularidad en el regreso a la competición ante el Villarreal, con Huijsen sancionado, Konaté lesionado (aunque todo apunta a que se recuperará a tiempo) y Militao en proceso de recibir el alta competitiva tras muchos meses sin jugar. En agosto, tras superar una lesión muscular, la dolencia en la tibia volvió a aparecer. Un problema (una pequeña fisura) que arrastra desde enero y que le ha torturado desde entonces. El tratamiento conservador no ha funcionado y tampoco las incontables sesiones específicas de trabajo con el objetivo de descargar y recuperar la zona afectada. Asencio quería ser una opción para Mou en un momento de apuro con los centrales e intentar ganarse la confianza del técnico, pero la lesión en la tibia no da tregua y obliga a tomar una decisión que puede ser inminente para recuperar nuevamente la mejor versión del defensa. Con el final de la temporada pasada llegaba el momento de descansar para Asencio, que arriesgó en la recta final para dar la cara junto al equipo y apurar sus opciones de estar en el Mundial. El plan durante el verano era sencillo: reposo, recuperación y dejar que el paso del tiempo permitiera a la zona regenerarse. La previsión era que la tibia respondiera al descanso después de meses de exigencia. Pero no ha ocurrido así. La situación de Asencio ha empeorado y la tibia vuelve a convertirse en una amenaza para su temporada. El problema pudo haberse agravado por la lesión en el cuádriceps de finales de julio, también en la misma pierna, que le obligó a modificar sus cargas y su trabajo durante la pretemporada.

articles.title: Man City Premier League charges: Appeal process, punishment hearing and what happens now after guilty verdict
articles.summary: Man City have been found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission; City were charged by the Premier League with more than 100 breaches in February 2023
articles.body:
Manchester City have confirmed they will appeal the ruling . They have until Friday October 2 to do so.

The appeal - which is permitted under section W of the Premier League rules.- would be heard by a new three-person commission.

Can sanctions be imposed while an appeal is under way?

There will be a separate hearing with the independent commission to determine sanctions. It is unclear when this hearing will take place but, reading between the lines, the Premier League wants this concluded this season.

The Premier League will put forward what they think the punishment should be and City will argue their case. The commission will then go away and decide what the punishment should be.

Would the appeal be the end of the matter?

The appeal would be the end of this part of the process.

City cannot appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS). But they could go to the High Court and argue that the process has not been fair and impartial.

There could also be more legal cases, with clubs potentially taking action against City over missing out on trophies and Champions League qualification.

There are a range of sanctions available to the independent commission which include fines, points deductions and other sporting sanctions - which could be applied this season.

The Premier League do not have set sanctions for financial rule breaches. Clubs decided not to have them because there were fears clubs would break the rules and just take the punishment if they knew what the punishment was going to be.

In February 2025, Richard Masters, the Premier League chief executive, said the league was looking at having a sanctions grid - setting out agreed sanctions for different rules breaches.

Everton were deducted six points on appeal during the 2023/24 season and then two points for profit and sustainability rules (PSR) breaches. Nottingham Forest were deducted four points in the same season.

In the 2008/09 season, Luton were deducted 30 points (10 points for illegal payments to agents and 20 points for exiting administration without a Company Voluntary Arrangement ) .

In 2021/22 season, Derby were deducted 21 points (12 points for entering administration and nine points for financial irregularities).

Manchester City can only end up in the Championship if they are given a significant enough points penalty which means they go on to be relegated from the PL.

What happens if City are expelled from the Premier League?

Expulsion means they are no longer a Premier League (PL) club. It does NOT mean that they have been relegated.

City will then have to go to The Football Association and apply to rejoin the football pyramid further down.

Then the problem of re-integration lies with The FA and English Football League.

The FA will have a huge part to play in deciding where City play their football next, in this scenario. Where that might be is unknown, and very complicated and political.

Will the Premier League decide to negate all City's results for this season because it has happened mid-season? It's something they will have to decide upon.

Written into the EFL laws: any new member who joins EFL, has to join at League Two.

The EFL, like the Premier League, is a collective of its member clubs, and so any decision to re-enter Man City at a certain level (any level from the Championship or below) would have to be ratified by a vote of the member clubs.

If it went to a vote, it would be passed or rejected on a simple majority, a vote that involves all 72 EFL clubs.

That was the system for when the Championship play-offs were expanded from 4-6 teams last season - it required a majority of the 72 AND a specific majority of the Championship clubs.

Will clubs in any division be keen for a club of Man City's power to join their league?

City released a statement stating they are "disappointed and surprised" after the club were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules.

"Manchester City is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League commission that has been published today.

"The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.

El City es un valor añadido para nosotros, pero no somos jueces y no estamos en posición por ahora de juzgar. Tú dices que hicieron trampas, pero ellos dicen que no. articles.title: Man City guilty of almost all the 115 financial charges, Premier League says
articles.summary: Manchester City has been found guilty of almost all of the unprecedented 115 charges of financial wrongdoing it faced, the Premier League confirmed on Tuesday, in one of the biggest scandals in English soccer history.
articles.body: Manchester City has been found guilty of almost all of the unprecedented 115 charges of financial wrongdoing it faced, the Premier League confirmed on Tuesday, in one of the biggest scandals in English soccer history. City, the most successful team in England for the past 15 years and the current Premier League leader, now faces severe sanctions that could include a huge points deduction or even expulsion from the world’s most popular soccer league, causing huge reputational damage to its Abu Dhabi ownership. The explosive verdict by an independent commission — which was reported by a number of British media outlets on Friday — “details how the club systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade,” Premier League chief executive Richard Masters said in a case that was initiated by the competition more than three years ago and first arose in 2018 from leaked club emails and documents. City said it was “disappointed and surprised” by the commission’s verdict, that it was “innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League” and will be “relentless” as it pursues avenues to appeal. City was accused of a raft of financial violations from 2009-18 — a period when the northwest club, long in the shadow of great rival Manchester United, was transforming itself into a record-breaking global superpower that has won multiple Premier League titles and the Champions League. The violations included failing to provide accurate financial information and submitting inflated figures for sponsorship deals out of Abu Dhabi, hiding payments that supplemented the salaries of managers and players, and breaching financial rules established by the Premier League and UEFA, European soccer’s governing body, aiming to keep clubs financially stable by not spending beyond their means. On top of that, City faced many other charges of failing to cooperate with the investigation between 2018-23. “An independent commission has found Manchester City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-season period,” the league said, “and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the league’s investigation.” Regarding the sponsorship deals, the league said: “Manchester City arranged ‘sham’ contracts (which misrepresented the true agreement between the parties) with a number of its commercial partners, as well as relying on ‘sham’ agreements with others, to artificially inflate the club’s revenues and reduce its costs. “The club,” the league added, “filed misstated accounts and concealed the true state of its finances from its auditors and football regulators.” The purpose of City’s “schemes” was found to have been to “artificially inflate the club’s revenues, and reduce its costs, by more than £900 million ($1.19 billion) during the affected period, to appear to comply with financial rules,” the league said. The finding suggests that City’s rise to the top of the English game, fueled by investments from Abu Dhabi that delivered by its expensively assembled, star-studded squads, was achieved at lest in part by evading the league’s financial regulations. The Premier League said sanctions will be decided in a separate hearing held by the independent commission. Any appeal by City would have to be made by Friday, the league said. Tuesday’s verdict is set to bring chaos to English soccer in general, triggering a slew of lawsuits from rival clubs calling for compensation for having been impacted by City’s actions. There’s also the question of whether City’s top stars, like Erling Haaland and Rayan Cherki, will stay at the club and what the future holds for Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan. He is the deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates and a member of Abu Dhabi’s royal family who bought City in 2008 and has gone on to own a group of worldwide teams — under the City Football Group banner — including New York City FC and Melbourne City. City has always protested its innocence in the case, saying in 2023 when the charges were laid that there was a “comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence that exists in support of its position.” Even over the weekend, City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said there remained a “confidence and intent in proving the club’s innocence.” The appeal could end up in the High Court in London if City feels the process in the case was unfair and/or impartial.

articles.title: Los 1.050 millones de euros que el City se ahorró "haciendo trampas": se lo gastó en estos fichajes
articles.standfirst: La Comisión independiente ha declarado al Manchester City culpable de todos los cargos relacionados con graves infracciones de las normas financieras
articles.summary: Una Comisión independiente ha declarado al Manchester City FC culpable de todos los cargos, reduciendo sus costes en más de 900 millones de libras
articles.body: La Premier League se acaba de posicionar respecto al caso del Manchester City. Oficializan la culpabilidad del equipo de todos los cargos relacionados con graves infracciones de las normas financieras de la Premier League durante un periodo de nueve temporadas, y la mayoría de los cargos relacionados con su falta de cooperación con la investigación de la Liga. Entre algunas de las conclusiones, señalaron que el City "organizó contratos 'falsos' e incumplió significativamente los límites de gasto tanto de la Premier League como de la UEFA". El objetivo del club, en palabras de la Premier, era "reducir sus costes en más de 900 millones de libras (1.050 millones de euros) durante el periodo afectado, para parecer que cumplían con las normas financieras". La consecuencia de esto, según la Comisión, fue que "el club presentó cuentas erróneas y ocultó el verdadero estado financiero a sus auditores y reguladores del fútbol". La Comisión independiente determinó que el Manchester City realizó acuerdos comerciales ficticios con varios de sus patrocinadores durante ese período, como parte de un esquema de financiación encubierto, mediante el cual dichas empresas solo debían pagar una parte de las tarifas de patrocinio correspondientes. El resto fue financiado por Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd (ADUG), propietaria del club. Como parte de este esquema, se formalizaron otros acuerdos ficticios, financiados por ADUG, para que el club pudiera registrar gastos operativos inferiores a los reales, así como un acuerdo circular ficticio con Fordham, una entidad que adquirió los derechos de imagen de los jugadores del club, financiado también por ADUG. Y durante esos años, desde la 09/10 hasta la 17/18, el equipo se gastó 1.440 millones de euros, gracias a los cuales llegaron a Mánchester grandes figuras que han logrado cambiar la historia del club.

articles.title: Al Fursan-led consortium acquires Kerala Blasters FC from Magnum Group
articles.summary: KOCHI: A consortium led by UAE-based Al Fursan Group has taken complete ownership of Kerala Blasters FC, one of the most popular clubs in the Indian Super
articles.body: KOCHI: A consortium led by UAE-based Al Fursan Group has taken complete ownership of Kerala Blasters FC, one of the most popular clubs in the Indian Super League. The announcement was made at a news conference in Kochi on Tuesday. Club officials did not disclose the value of the transaction, but sources indicate that the deal is worth about Rs 120 crore, placing it among the largest foreign investments in Indian football in recent years.The takeover ends the tenure of Hyderabad-based Magnum Sports, which had owned and managed the club since 2016. Kerala Blasters CEO Abhik Chatterjee said the ownership transfer will be carried out in phases and is expected to be completed over the next eight months.Under the new arrangement, the club’s operations will be managed by Ofioh Sporty. Its CEO, Thameem Anvar, said the new owners have plans to develop a dedicated stadium for the Blasters. He added that more details would be revealed once “Project Blasters” is formally announced.There had been speculation that the club could shift its base to Kozhikode, but Chatterjee clarified that Kochi will remain Kerala Blasters’ home. The team will continue to play its home matches at the Jawaharlal Nehru International Stadium. Addressing expectations for the upcoming season, he said the club’s ambition to win remains strong, though preparations are limited by time. He also confirmed that Ashley Westwood will continue as head coach and will take decisions on squad matters.Chatterjee dismissed reports suggesting that the Blasters’ opening home match could be postponed. He said delaying the fixture would be unfair to other teams because the league schedule has already been released.Al Fursan Group is understood to have backing from business interests connected to Sharjah’s ruling Al Qasimi family. Its entry gives a Gulf-based investment group control of a club with one of the largest fan bases in Indian football.The acquisition comes as Kerala Blasters prepare for the 2026-27 ISL season. articles.summary: El CEO del club no quiso hacer declaraciones públicas tras la oficialidad del veredicto
articles.body: Ferran Soriano, consejero delegado del Manchester City, se dirigió a los empleados del club en un vídeo en el que dice que las acusaciones de irregularidades financieras de la Premier League están basadas en falsedades y tildó de "teoría de la conspiración" la posición de la liga inglesa. El directivo, que no quiso hablar en la asamblea general de clubes celebrada en Copenhague, sí se dirigió a los empleados del club en un momento de mucha incertidumbre después de que la Premier League confirmara que son culpables de la mayoría de cargos de los que le acusa desde febrero de 2023. "La totalidad del caso con la Premier League está basado en una falsa acusación, que es lo que el dinero de nuestros dueños fue puesto en el club a través de algunos patrocinadores de Abu Dhabi. Esto no es verdad y se ha dado las suficientes pruebas a la comisión de la Premier League de que esto no pasó y que no va a pasar. Hablamos de extractos bancarios, transferencias de dinero, testigos y todo lo necesario para demostrar de forma categórica que el dinero no vino del dueño". "Todo falso cargo contra nosotros viene de esta simple y completa falsa acusación. Sorprendentemente tanto para nosotros como para nuestros abogados, después de más de dos años, la comisión de la Premier League ha dado una opinión que apoya la teoría de la conspiración de la Premier. Para ello, se han ignorado las pruebas que ha dado el club y se ha llegado a una conclusión que es errónea". En el vídeo, Soriano confirma que el club apelará, como ya había dejado claro en un comunicado previo. Ahora, es cuestión de que la comisión independiente determinará cuál es la sanción adecuada para el City, pudiendo ir esta desde una multa económica, hasta la pérdida de puntos, descenso de categoría o expulsión de la liga. articles.title: Deion Sanders, Colorado Reportedly Expected to Bench Julian Lewis, Make QB Change
articles.summary: Colorado might be eyeing a quarterback change.
articles.body:
Colorado might be eyeing a quarterback change.

According to Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports, the Buffs are "currently expected" to bench Julian Lewis and promote Isaac Wilson to starter.

Head coach Deion Sanders was coy on the matter, however, saying he hasn't decided on a starter this week.

In eight career games over the past two seasons, Lewis, a former 4-star recruit, has thrown for 1,322 yards, 10 touchdowns and two interceptions, completing 59.8 percent of his passes while taking 20 sacks. But Colorado is just 3-5 in his starts over the past two years, including 2-2 this season.

Against Baylor on Saturday, he finished 11-of-16 for just 76 yards while taking three sacks in a 23-13 loss. He was benched at halftime in favor of Wilson, who finished 12-of-25 passes for 156 yards and a score.

"We ran the ball well in the first half—that's about it," Sanders told reporters regarding the quarterback switch. "I'll take the responsibility for the decision that I made because I was trying to get us going."

Sanders seems more than comfortable turning to Wilson—or even third-stringer Kaneal Sweetwyne—if necessary.

"Isaac had a great spring. I don't know if you guys remember that," he told reporters Tuesday. "If he gets the nod, I feel all out that he's going to do his thing. Sweetwyne, as well... I love what he brings to the table."

articles.title: Former Auburn Staffer Faces Felony Charges for Allegedly Stealing and Sharing Trade Secrets
articles.summary: AUBURN, Ala. (AP) — A former Auburn staffer has been arrested on charges of stealing trade secrets from the football program and sending them to competitors, according to court records.
articles.body:
AUBURN, Ala. (AP) — A former Auburn staffer has been arrested on charges of stealing trade secrets from the football program and sending them to competitors, according to court records.

David Rudolph Jenrath, 24, turned himself in to authorities Monday and was charged with two felonies: theft of trade secrets and computer tampering. He is being held on $15,000 bond at the Lee County Jail, according to police.

A news release issued Tuesday by the Auburn Police Department said a "business reported that sensitive information was stolen from the business and distributed to their competitors. The business reported that one of their competitors received the information and turned it over to them."

It's unclear which schools received the stolen information. A complaint alleges that the incident occurred on July 19 at the Auburn Athletics Complex.

Jenrath's profile on LinkedIn, which has now been removed, said he worked for the Auburn football program as a player personnel scouting assistant from January through June. His focus was on running backs and special teams.

His profile said his duties included evaluating high school and transfer-portal prospects, preparing scouting reports and recruiting summaries, assisting with opponent scouting and maintaining recruiting databases. His profile also said he was an applied artificial intelligence/sports analytics student at the University of Tennessee.

articles.title: Man City charges verdict - key findings: 'The Fordham Arrangement' effectively a front for Abu Dhabi United Group
articles.summary: Man City will appeal the findings of the independent commission following the publication of a 40-page document which reveals 'sham' deals, 'dishonest' witnesses and details of 'The Fordham Arrangement', described as being "little more than a front" for Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG)
articles.body:
Manchester City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

The charge that was not proven was regarding one element of the Premier League's non-cooperation case.

The independent commission repeatedly concluded that a number of City's commercial agreements were "shams" and "far in excess" of fair market value.

City used a "Disguised Funding Scheme" where Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) partially funded sponsorship fees from Abu Dhabi sponsors.

As a result, the club's financial statements showed their commercial income from Abu Dhabi sponsors was £949.94m from 2009-10 to 2017-18.

In reality, the Abu Dhabi sponsors only paid £119.25m to City over that period, and the remaining £830.69m was paid by ADUG.

"By using the Disguised Funding Scheme at the very end of the 2009/10 financial year", the commission's report read, "the club was able to avoid breaking the record for the largest single-season loss in Premier League history".

City tried to 'obscure' realities of finances

The commission's report shows how City unsuccessfully argued against the Disguised Funding Scheme.

City said Abu Dhabi sponsors were liable for the amounts stated in their financial reports, but from time to time these sponsors would apply for financial support from the Abu Dhabi government.

The commission rejected City's explanation, which it concluded had been "concocted well after the event in an attempt to obscure and conceal the realities of the Disguised Funding Scheme".

The commission concluded that City's financial statements for the seasons between 2009-10 and 2017-18 "did not show a true and fair view" of the club's financial position.

The commission's report also mentions three separate remuneration agreements that were omitted from City's accounts and paid by ADUG worth nearly £17m.

City used a third party, Fordham, as a device to overstate income by £24.5m and understate expenses by £49.414m.

The commission described 'The Fordham Arrangement' as being "little more than a front for ADUG".

The Fordham Arrangement was, the commission contended, "a further device by which ADUG funds could be paid into the club in a manner that concealed their true origin" and which enabled "the club to remove operating expenses from its financial statements".

The Fordham Arrangement was part of a system called 'Project Longbow' which "was a multi-strand project whose purpose was to explore how the club might boost its revenues and reduce its operating losses".

But while "many of the strands of Project Longbow were genuine, legitimate attempts to achieve those aims. One was not. That was the Fordham Arrangement".

The independent commission heard factual evidence from 27 witnesses over 42 days in the last quarter of 2024, with a core bundle of key documents running to "many tens of thousands of pages".

The commission says the club made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the investigation.

It also found some witnesses on behalf of the club gave false evidence, while other City witnesses were found by the commission to give knowingly untrue evidence and so had been dishonest.

The commission found City had breached UEFA and Premier League financial rules, while also ruling that "by its conduct the club clearly intended to circumvent the PL rules".

The Premier League said it regarded City's conduct as having "extremely serious, significant, sustained and intentional or reckless breaches of rules critical to the proper and fair operation of the Premier League's league competition".

Manchester City have confirmed they will appeal against the ruling and have until Friday October 2 to do so.

articles.title: Perdonen, ¿cuándo es el próximo parón?
articles.standfirst: La contracrónica del España - Croacia
articles.summary: La contracrónica del España - Croacia
articles.body: El parón de selecciones siempre ha sido eso que llegaba cuando menos apetecía. Algo que molestaba, para ser sinceros. Justo cuando LaLiga cogía carrerilla, cuando la Champions empezaba a calentarse, cuando uno ya tenía controlado el ritmo del miércoles-domingo... Parón. Dos semanas mirando el calendario y preguntándose cuánto faltaba para que volviera el fútbol de verdad. En MARCA, de hecho, solo lo defendía Miguel Ángel Lara. Le llamábamos loco. Pues resulta que ahora el fútbol de verdad juega de rojo y que con esta España los parones ya no estorban. Es más, visto lo visto en este, se esperan. Casi se agradecen. Partidos como el de Croacia o como el de Inglaterra del pasado fin de semana han conseguido algo que hace no demasiado tiempo parecía complicado, que uno mire el calendario internacional con ganas. Y no es sólo porque España gane. Es por cómo juega. Por cómo sale a buscar al rival, por el hambre que tiene un equipo que acaba de ganar el Mundial y parece comportarse como si todavía no hubiera ganado nada. Jugadores y afición, que agota las entradas en pocos minutos, no quieren dejar ni las migajas a sus rivales. No hace mucho, los partidos de selecciones se veían, si es que se veían, casi por obligación. Porque jugaba España. Porque tocaba. Por inercia. Porque había que clasificarse a la competición de turno. Ahora apetece sentarse delante de la televisión para pasar un buen rato. Y en eso tiene mucho mérito, por no decir todo el mérito, Luis de la Fuente. Así que habrá que desterrar ya lo de que sobran los parones. Porque si el parón consiste en ver a esta España contra Croacia, Inglaterra o cualquiera que se ponga delante, igual el problema empieza a ser que se hace demasiado largo esperar hasta el siguiente. España empezó el partido con una jugada perfecta. 70 segundos. 25 pases. Un remate certero de Lamine pegado al palo. La tocaron todos los jugadores menos Unai y Fermín, que participó dejando pasar el balón, en un amague clave para que el balón le cayese a su compañero. Es la carta de presentación de España desde que es campeona del mundo. Lo hizo ante Inglaterra y repitió ante Croacia. Con Lamine como ejecutor del vertical y preciso juego de España. Fabián ha disputado 52 partidos con España y no ha perdido ninguno. Es récord ese 0% de derrotas con tal número de partidos, aunque la trayectoria más larga sin perder la tiene Marchena, que alcanzó los 57 partidos seguidos sin conocer la derrota. Se acerca Fabián a esa marca con un protagonismo y peso en la selección fundamentales. Porque se puede dar la vuelta a la visión y destacar que España nunca pierde con Fabián en el campo por todo lo que juega y equilibra al equipo. Un jugador descomunal. De la Fuente firmó el contrato de su vida cuando la mayoría de la población está pensando en la jubilación. Hasta 2032. Pero el acuerdo entre el seleccionador y la Federación debería de ser infinito. Hasta que él quiera. Porque estos jugadores que dominan el mundo con puño de hierro, reconozcámoslo, no nos parecían tan buenos hace cuatro años. "Nos faltan cracks", repetíamos una y otra vez. Y hoy estos mismos jugadores son los mejores del mundo sin discusión. Y el mérito es del entrenador, que ha armado un equipo con mayúsculas que ya mira cara a cara a la selección de Luis Aragonés y Vicente del Bosque. Las comparaciones siempre son injustas, pero el debate es inevitable. ¿Qué selección es mejor? Slaven Bilic reservó a Luka Modric en el banquillo pensando en la segunda parte y en los otros dos partidos de este parón, pero el encuentro acabó dejándole sin margen para cambiar su destino. Al menos, el seleccionador le concedió los últimos diez minutos para que se llevara el cariño de la afición. ¡Qué ovación cuando saltó al campo! ¡Y qué merecida! Modric siempre dice que lo más importante de su carrera es ese afecto, por encima de los títulos y los premios. "Los trofeos se quedan en una vitrina, el cariño de la gente te acompaña para siempre", dice el croata. Y Luka lo recibe incluso de quienes han sufrido su fútbol. Porque, como sucedió en su día con Iniesta, Modric también es patrimonio de la humanidad. España jugó los primeros 60 minutos al ritmo que marcó Zubimendi. Y no le fue nada mal al equipo. El Real Madrid se cerró en banda a firmar un mediocentro cuando se le cayó lo de Rodri, pero no le habría ido nada mal con Zubimendi. El mediocentro español ha perdido peso en el Arsenal, es cierto, pero quizás se deba más a la adaptación a la Premier que a su talento. Porque cada vez que juega con España lo borda. Con Rodri en el Barça, seguro que el madridismo habría celebrad un Zubimendi.

articles.title: Who continues to show how important they are? - England player ratings

articles.body:
England got their first win in the Nations League as Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane scored to beat the Czech Republic 2-0.

Here's how BBC Sport England reporter Alex Howell rated the players. You can see how you scored them below.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

James Trafford: Made a good save in the second half. Trafford was very calm with the ball at his feet and showed his passing range which pleased Tuchel throughout. 6

Trent Alexander-Arnold: Started his first England game for nearly two years. Not much to do defensively but put in a great ball for the England opener. 7

Trevoh Chalobah: A shaky start from the centre back who lost possession a couple of times and lost out in challenges which frustrated manager Thomas Tuchel. But Chalobah settled and ensured England kept a clean sheet against 10-man Czech Republic. 6

Marc Guehi: The usual reliable performance from Guehi. England didn't have much defending to do but he put in a couple of important blocks. 6

Lewis Hall: The left-back combined well with Anthony Gordon and offered a good outlet for England. Hall was a threat going forward and should have scored in the second half. 7

Elliot Anderson: Dominated the midfield, kept the ball ticking for England and won possession back the few times that the Czech Republic ventured forward. A mature performance. 7

Myles Lewis-Skelly: Started the game well and was given a lot of responsibility in England's build up play. However, Lewis-Skelly was booked for a mis-timed tackle and then taken off at half time. 6

Morgan Rogers: Played Bukayo Saka through with a nice pass early on and hit the post twice. Not given much room by a Czech side who defended very deep. 6

Bukayo Saka: Not much of note to mark for Saka in what was a cagey match as England laboured when breaking down the Czech defence before Gordon's goal. 6

Anthony Gordon: A constant threat in behind and put in a dangerous cross in the first half that deserved to end up with a goal. Scored the opener and continues to show why he is becoming so important for the Three Lions. 8

Harry Kane: A quieter night for Kane who dropped deep and went looking for the ball but the England captain still got on the score sheet with a good finish inside the area in the second half. 7

Eberechi Eze (on 46, Lewis-Skelly): Added a spark to midfield. 6

Jude Bellingham (on 70, Kane): Took the captains armband and led the line. 6

articles.title: Lamine Yamal es el dorado
articles.standfirst: El zurdo, con dos goles y una asistencia, pone el brillo en otro gran partido de España, que desfigura a Croacia
articles.summary: El zurdo, con dos goles y una asistencia, pone el brillo en otro gran partido de España, que desfigura a Croacia
articles.body: Hay partidos que empiezan en Lamine y terminan en Yamal. Una exhibición del zurdo en su autopista hacia el oro, dos goles y una asistencia, fue clave para que España mantenga el estado de felicidad. No hay forma de toser a los campeones del mundo, no hay manera de esposar a Lamine Yamal. Lo avisó Bilic, seleccionador croata, en la víspera del choque. La diferencia de la España del 2010 con esta se llama Lamine Yamal, un futbolista diferente. Pronto comprobaría que estaba cargado de razón. El primer campanazo lo dio con alguna butaca vacía; el segundo, antes de ser sustituido. La ovación se escuchó en Zagreb. El que confiese que no ve los partidos de España merece que su cara se pegue en las farolas, que se le expulse de los grupos de guasap y que no pueda sentarse en una terraza. Un partido de los campeones del mundo es una piscina de bolas, un producto de la industria del entretenimiento que hay que saborear cada segundo. La última moda para esta cofradía de descarados es marcar goles en el primer minuto. Da igual Wembley o el Pizjuán, esa sala de magia en la que España nunca ha perdido. Se sacó de centro y la selección se dispuso a oficiar un rondo gigante por todo el campo. El balón llegó a la izquierda, Cucurella conectó con Baena y el pase de este llegó a Lamine Yamal, que sabía por dónde iba a marcar antes de que le llegara la pelota. La recreación del gol, después de setenta segundos de toques, debería entrar cuanto antes en una estancia de la Ciudad del Fútbol de Las Rozas. De la Fuente había apostado de iniciar por remover algunas piezas. En la comandancia, Zubimendi ocupó el puesto de Rodri; en la mediapunta, Fermín entró por Olmo; en la defensa, Huijsen relegó a Laporte. Pedri continúa como símbolo del Plan B, una extrañeza que sólo se puede permitir España. No hacía falta mucho más. Tras el gol, Fermín activó el modo torbellino. Jugó cada minuto como si se acordara de lo que se había perdido en el Mundial. Fermín dio trabajo a los jardineros para arreglar el césped de las zonas que pisaba. España había reducido a Croacia a un club de ajedrez. El balón era un objeto desconocido en un grupo que acusaba la ausencia de Modric en la foto inicial. En esas atmósferas de superioridad una chispa enciende hogueras. Baena se empeñó de forma innecesaria en buscar la amarilla. La encontró mientras los croatas le hacían un escáner. No se descompuso ni cuando los croatas igualaron en su primer intento, un cabezazo de Beljo a centro de Perisic. Sin tiempo para el enfado, Pubill cabeceó a la red un envío envuelto en celofán de Yamal con la pierna derecha... Exclusivas del Pizjuán. De la Fuente está en uno de esos momentos en los que se encuentra un boleto premiado sin pasar por el despacho. Todo lo que decide le sale bien. Cuando entró Pedri por Fermín se recobró el control del balón. El canario hiló un pase sobre Lamine Yamal en la banda derecha. Se metió en el área y colocó el balón en los únicos centímetros que había entre Livakovic y el primer palo. Una genialidad aunque se pidiera al croata que tapara mejor su cocina. Un vicio moderno es buscar un culpable en cada gol. El extremo se sentó a continuación encima del balón. Después fue sustituido por Víctor Muñoz. Croacia deseaba que todo acabara cuanto antes. Faltaba el premio al señorío, la ovación a Modric al entrar en el terreno de juego. En el tiempo de los bises, Nico Williams remachó el último gol del partido. A veces no se añora LaLiga. Es el mérito de España.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal: ¿Una muesca más para el Balón de Oro? Otra más"
articles.standfirst: El MVP del España - Croacia atendió a los medios tras la victoria de la Selección
articles.summary: El MVP del España - Croacia atendió a los medios tras la victoria de la Selección
articles.body: Lamine Yamal fue la gran figura del 4-1 de España a Croacia en el Sánchez-Pizjuán, con dos goles y una asistencia. El extremo explicó su primer tanto, un disparo ajustado al palo corto de Livakovic: "Ya lo conozco de los entrenos, he pensado en los entrenos, en lo que hace él y me ha entrado". El futbolista abrió el marcador en los primeros minutos y firmó el 3-1 en la segunda parte, en una noche en la que la selección estrenó como local la segunda estrella y encadenó su 40º partido sin perder. El jugador también valoró el ambiente vivido en Sevilla y el objetivo del equipo de cara al Mundial de 2026: "Nos da mucha ilusión poder traer la copa aquí y enseñársela a la afición y poder ganar y traerlo a casa pues genial". Preguntado por si su actuación suponía un nuevo argumento en su candidatura al Balón de Oro, Lamine Yamal respondió sin dudar un solo segundo: "Otra más". En zona mixta, Lamine Yamal insistió en la importancia del arranque, después de un gol muy tempranero: "Hay que salir enchufados siempre, lo que nos dice el míster, lo que hablamos entre nosotros y muy contento por la victoria". El extremo restó trascendencia al debate sobre el Balón de Oro, cuya votación ya se ha cerrado: "Al final no solo juego para este Balón de Oro, juego para mí, para la afición, para la siguiente temporada, para mi selección, para seguir ganando". Preguntado por si la actuación le acercaba al premio, zanjó: "No lo sé, no voto yo, ni sé quién ha ganado, no sé nada. A esperar y a seguir jugando". El futbolista se mostró especialmente satisfecho con su estado de forma y su momento personal. "Ya dije antes del partido del Feyenoord que es el momento donde más feliz estoy y estoy disfrutando mucho", señaló el jugador, que apareció suelto y sonriente sobre el césped del Sánchez-Pizjuán en una de sus mejores noches con la selección.

articles.title: Hundreds attend controversial Mulbarton v Woodford FA Cup replay
articles.summary: The controversial replay follows the FA ruling a referee had made a mistake in the initial match.
articles.body:
Village football club Mulbarton Wanderers saw off lower league rivals Woodford Town to settle a controversial FA Cup replay.

The first meeting of the teams made international headlines after the Football Association (FA) made the rare decision to order a replay due to a referee's error.

A record crowd of 806 people attended the match in Norfolk this evening, with Wanderers sealing progress thanks to a 2-0 win.

The victory brings with it £3,375 from the FA Cup prize fund and a home tie against Gloucester City in the third qualifying round of the world's oldest football competition.

Mulbarton had to introduce advance ticketing because of "unprecedented demand" due to the attention.

That followed a surprise decision by the FA to rule that the game should be replayed and switched to Norfolk.

London club Woodford, who play in a league below Mulbarton, lodged an appeal due to the laws of the game being applied incorrectly during the initial game, which Wanderers had won 2-1.

With the match still at 0-0 in the first half, Woodford had a penalty disallowed for their players encroaching into the penalty area.

However, the game was restarted with Mulbarton being awarded a free-kick, instead of Woodford being able to retake the penalty.

Speaking before the game, Danny Self, joint first team manager at Mulbarton, said: "There's all the emotions, you ask questions and you're frustrated.

"Then you ask can we appeal this and you're told you can't.

"Whether we agree or disagree, we are where we are and we've just got to prepare for it."

Dan Robathan, a retired Premier League and FIFA referee, defended the original matchday official.

He said: "There's a misconception that when we make a decision, that we don't care which is so far from the truth.

"It hits you quite personally and you don't want to have a negative effect on a game.

"But you're trying to process all that at once and I can only assume he's got confused with the law in that moment."

The village club, around six miles (10km) south of Norwich, has risen through local leagues in recent years and is competing at step four of the non-league pyramid for the first time this season.

The tie against Gloucester in the next round is scheduled for the weekend of Saturday 3 October.

Gloucester play at step three of non-league, in Southern League Premier Division South. The winner will claim £5,625 in winnings and the losers £1,875.

Despite losing tonight's tie, Woodford also collect £1,125 from the prize fund.

articles.body:
Scotland were well beaten by Switzerland in their second Nations League match, as the visitors cruised to victory in Sebastian Pocognoli's first home game in charge.

Jack Hendry's 11th-minute red card proved too much for the Scots to overcome as they fell to a 3-0 defeat.

Here's how we rated Scotland's players - and you can give your marks below.

Angus Gunn – Beaten on his side of the goal by Ricardo Rodriguez's powerful free-kick for the opening goal. Good saves either side of half-time to deny Ndoye, but beaten by power again for Zeki Amdouni's third goal. 4

Jack Hendry – Roasted for pace by Dan Ndoye and clumsily brought the striker down to earn a deserved red card, leaving Scotland down to 10 early on. 2

Luis Binks – Brondby defender's first act was a rash late tackle. Slow to close down Ndoye and prevent the cross that set up Nico Elvedi for Switzerland's second goal, but otherwise did not look out of place. 6

Andy Robertson – Usual willingness to get up and down the left flank yielded little reward on his 99th Scotland appearance. 6

articles.title: Manchester City charges: The intricate web spun to con the Premier League
articles.summary: The 40-page document which confirmed Manchester City were found guilty of inflating sponsorship income makes fascinating reading. Here's what it sets out.
articles.body:
"To cheat, trick, deceive, delude with false pretences; to impose upon, take in, hoax."

That is the Oxford English definition of the word "sham".

And that word appears eight times in the independent commission's ruling published on Tuesday , which found Manchester City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of financial rules, and all but one in relation to a failure to co-operate with the investigation.

The 40-page document makes fascinating reading.

It catalogues how the club's owners, Abu Dhabi United Group, knew from the 2009-10 season that there would be major overspends if the club was to reach the level they wanted to get to.

So, the ruling says, City found a way to boost sponsorship income. Season, after season, after season.

The report shows how the club's owners were topping up the value of the deals.

The so-called Disguised Funding Scheme is the central plank in a series of charges that Manchester City have been found guilty of by the Premier League.

This scheme managed to hide more than £830m of sponsorship funding, while other devices hid £90m in expenses.

We break down the key findings from the document.

The problem became apparent very quickly for the new owners

Manchester City were bought by Abu Dhabi investors in 2008 but, the document says, their predicament had become clear from the start of the 2009-10 season.

These were ambitious new owners who did not just want the club to be competitive. They wanted to have the best players and be winners.

That was not going to be possible without spending more money. And lots of it.

Total losses for the 2009-10 campaign were going to exceed what was, at that time, the record single-season financial loss by a Premier League member club. That was Chelsea FC in 2006, of £140m.

According to the ruling, that was a record that the City owners were adamant the club should not break

The club knew they would likely continue to suffer large losses for at least the following five seasons.

This was when both Uefa and the Premier League were about to bring in financial fair play rules.

To address this the only option was to significantly increase commercial revenue - and reduce the reliance on their owners.

Sham contracts and the disguised funding scheme

In early 2010, Manchester City took the first steps to get the additional funding into the club.

City would enter into sponsorship agreements which were record amounts and were significantly above fair market value.

It is referred to as the 'disguised funding scheme'.

This is how it worked, according to the ruling.

The sponsorship deals were split into two parts: a base fee, and a tagged sum.

And the club's owners would pay the tagged sum.

Ergo, the sponsors would not have to pay the full value of the contract. The club's owners would pay the vast majority, which enabled them to invest in players.

This, the document states, "gave the misleading impression to third parties (including regulators and its auditors) in its financial statements and any required FFP returns that its commercial revenues from sponsorship agreements were far, far greater than was in fact the case".

But the club also knew they had to be nimble.

From time to time the disguised funding scheme would be tweaked to "assist with continued concealment" and "reduce the likelihood of difficult questions being asked".

Commercial income from sponsors totalled £949.94m in the seasons from 2009-10 to 2017-18.

The ruling says only £119.25 million represented base fees.

A total of £830.69 million represented tagged sums - the amount paid by the club's owners.

Man City have denied the claims and say the Premier League had misunderstood the sponsorship agreements.

However, the panel said it "rejected that explanation as untrue".

It said it was "concocted well after the event in an attempt to obscure and conceal the realities of the disguised funding scheme".

An example given of the disguised funding scheme in action: plugging an unexpected shortfall in May 2013.

Less than a week before the end of that 2012-13 financial year the club knew they were £9.9m short of complying with Uefa's financial rules.

In a matter of days, without sponsors even being approached, a number of modified sponsor agreements were generated which increased recorded sponsorship fees to pay bonuses for events that had already taken place and to pay for a US tour.

The feared Uefa FFP shortfall was thus "plugged".

Football Daily: Premier League confirm Man City guilty of all charges - 5 Live reaction

In 2012, City launched what it called Project Longbow.

The ruling does say many of the strands of Project Longbow were genuine, and legitimate attempts to achieve the aims of boostings revenues and reducing operating losses.

One strand was not genuine, according to the ruling: the Fordham Arrangement.

This was an agreement between City and a third party called Fordham which was, according to the ruling, "little more than a front".

Funds from the club's owners "would be used (and were used) to enable Fordham to acquire from the club (at a sizeable, artificially-inflated price) the club's entitlement to benefit financially from its players' image rights".

It was a "further device by which funds could be paid into the club in a manner that concealed their true origin".

And this "enabled the club to pretend that such funds represented operating income".

In the financial statements wrongly recorded as operating income was the sum of £24.5m, and £49.414m was wrongly excluded from operating expenses.

The ruling says said the Fordham Arrangement was "operated with the knowledge and approval" of a number of individuals whose names were redacted.

Another way the club attempted to pass the financial rules was to move expensive contracts for players and managers off the books.

This was done by paying remuneration, or wages, through third parties. In reality this was being paid by the owners.

This was "instead recorded in a consultancy agreement" and "concealed the true extent of the club's liabilities".

There are three separate cases attributed to this, with all names redacted from the document. These may be published when the full written reasons are released.

City used this method for payments of £8.866m, £7.4m and £0.5m.

City's witnesses 'lied knowingly' during inquiry

"By its conduct the club clearly intended to circumvent the Premier League rules.

"The club made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the Premier League investigation".

This is another damning section, which brings into question the integrity of undisclosed people associated with City.

City served witness statements or documentary evidence from 24 individuals, most of whom who gave evidence at the hearing.

This could be problematic at a later date, as the new Independent Football Regulator is able to look at the honesty of integrity of directors and owners.

At present, no one has been named so we do not know the position of the people the ruling referred to.

It said that the evidence given by a number of important factual witnesses "was false in a number of key respects".

It added that certain factual witnesses provided evidence "that they knew to be untrue and so had been dishonest".

The ruling also said that City knew that the annual accounts "did not provide a true and fair view of the financial position" and that the club "was reckless as to whether those annual accounts provided a true and fair view".

All in this, it was said, showed that City failed to act "with utmost good faith" and "breached duties of co-operation that it owed to the Premier League".

This is how the club's financial statements for the seasons between 2009-10 and 2017-18 did not show a true and fair view of the financial position:

Wrongly recorded as operating income £24.5m

Wrongly excluded expenses totalling £49.414m

articles.title: La selección devuelve el precio de la entrada
articles.standfirst: Al otro lado del espejo
articles.summary: Al otro lado del espejo
articles.body: Contaba ayer aquí que no quedaba papel en Sevilla, tampoco lo hay para el sábado en Oviedo (ante Chequia), ni para el del 15-N en el Metropolitano (contra Inglaterra). Hoy toca decir que esta selección devuelve el precio de la entrada con el formidable espectáculo que despliega y, podríamos decir, por la forma en que asegura la alegría de un buen resultado. Anoche despachó con un 4-1 a Croacia, equipo serio y duro, al que desarboló en los primeros 20 minutos de una manera impresionante. Ese arranque emparentó con el de Londres, pues abrió enseguida el marcador Lamine (que está de dulce, al nivel de aquellas semifinales de la penúltima temporada ante el Inter) y luego se masticó una goleada que no llegó a producirse. Un tramo de juego excelso, rápido y profundo, con Baena tocando el violín, Fermín hecho un titán y Cucurella subiendo por la banda como acostumbraba antes de llegar al Madrid. Croacia tuvo el mérito de aguantar el chaparrón, equilibrar el partido y hasta alcanzar el empate. Es un equipo con cuajo. Tiene juego, tiene espíritu, tiene en Perisic un héroe que arrastra al equipo. El gigante Beljo marcó con un cabezazo imponente, pero España no dejó que se le secara encima el empate, porque enseguida vino el 2-1 por medio de Pubill, otro titán, que cabeceó un centro con música de Lamine. Con la derecha, por cierto. En algún otro se podría decir que ‘con su pierna mala’, pero mejor digamos que con la ‘menos buenísima’. Ya en la segunda mitad, antes de que se precipitaran los cambios, marcó el 3-1. Dos goles, una asistencia y una docena de diabluras Misión complida. El 4-1 lo marcaría Nico Williams, en una maniobra que nos permitió verle de nuevo pleno de salud, fuerza y confianza. Fue una noche grata en todos los sentidos. De nuevo un desfile de jugadores, entre novedades respecto al once inicial de Wembley y el preceptivo aluvión de cambios tras la primera hora de juego sin que el funcionamiento se alterara lo más mínimo. Y una nota feliz y emotiva: la aparición final de Modric, aplaudidísimo por el Sánchez Pizjuán.
