articles.title: Un parón para sanar: "Fue bastante duro para mí, pero lo importante es estar de vuelta"
articles.standfirst: Fermín, ausente en el Mundial por lesión, y Huijsen, descartado por decisión técnica, reaparecieron con la selección en el 4-1 a Croacia; Nico Williams, campeón del mundo, firmó el cuarto gol
articles.summary: Fermín, ausente en el Mundial por lesión, y Huijsen, descartado por decisión técnica, reaparecieron con la selección en el 4-1 a Croacia; Nico Williams, campeón del mundo, firmó el cuarto gol
articles.body: El presente parón de septiembre tuvo lectura de reencuentro para varios integrantes de la selección. Fermín López y Dean Huijsen, que se quedaron fuera de la lista del Mundial —el centrocampista por lesión y el central por decisión técnica—, volvieron a vestirse de rojo como titulares en el Sánchez-Pizjuán, mientras que Nico Williams, sí presente en la cita mundialista, está aprovechando la ventana para recuperar sensaciones con un gol. Fermín vivió una noche especial. "Un orgullo, era mi primer partido de titular y después de la lesión muy contento y un orgullo jugar para mi país", señaló en Teledeporte el jugador del Barcelona, que se estrenó como titular con España tras superar los problemas físicos que le apartaron de la fase final. "Han sido meses duros y estoy muy feliz de estar con la selección", añadió. El centrocampista tuvo alguna ocasión que no llegó a materializar. "No ha entrado pero lo he intentado, lo importante es que el equipo ha hecho un gran equipo", apuntó. Sobre cómo vivió el Mundial desde fuera, reconoció el punto agridulce: "Un poco raro, lo viví como un aficionado, estaba muy feliz pero tenía eso ahí de que podía haber estado pero ya he pasado página". Fermín valoró también el trato en su regreso al grupo: "Muy contento, como siempre, la verdad que Luis confía en mí, los compañeros conozco a muchos". Huijsen, por su parte, restó importancia a haberse quedado fuera y puso el foco en el nivel de exigencia del grupo. "Creo que eran los mismos en marzo y ahora, no han cambiado, tienen la misma exigencia de antes y queremos seguir ganando", afirmó el central en Teledeporte. Minutos después, reconoció lo doloroso que fue ese episodio a pregunta de MARCA en zona mixta: "Fue bastante duro para mí, fue un momento triste para mí y mi familia, pero lo importante es estar de vuelta". El defensa analizó el único tanto encajado, obra de Beljo. "Nos meten un centro lateral, meten bastante gente en área pero no estaban rematando casi nada", explicó sobre la acción que puso el 1-1 momentáneo. Formó pareja en el eje de la zaga con Cubarsí, sociedad de la que hizo una valoración escueta: "Bien, a seguir así y ya está". Distinto fue el caso de Nico Williams, campeón del mundo el pasado verano, que salió desde el banquillo y firmó el 4-1 definitivo. "Muy feliz por los tres puntos, por contribuir a la victoria del equipo y este gol me sirve para coger confianza", explicó el extremo del Athletic, que asumió con naturalidad su papel de suplente: "Como dice el míster, da igual quien juegue, que somos jugadores con mucha calidad. Baena el otro día hizo un trabajo espectacular que nos sirvió para remontar en Wembley y hoy me ha tocado a mí". El atacante recordó con nostalgia la conquista mundialista y deseó suerte a Lamine Yamal de cara al Balón de Oro. "Lo recuerdo con mucho cariño, no ha pasado tanto. Ganar un Mundial ya sabes lo que es, toda España vino a apoyarnos", rememoró Nico, antes de volcarse con su compañero: "Que sea el mismo y disfrute, cuando Lamine sonríe juega mejor. Es un jugador especial, el Balón de Oro no depende de él pero que siga jugando así y ojalá lo gane".

articles.title: Yamal stars as Spain thrash Croatia
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal scores twice and assists another as Spain beat Croatia 4-1 in UEFA Nations League Group A3
articles.body:
Lamine Yamal scored twice as World Cup winners Spain extended their European record unbeaten run to 40 matches.

La Roja maintained their perfect start to UEFA Nations League Group A3 with a 4-1 home win over Croatia on Tuesday, while England overcame 10-man Czech Republic 2-0 in Prague to leapfrog Slaven Bilic’s side into second.

In a repeat of the 2023 Nations League final, which Spain won on penalties, Croatia recovered from conceding an early goal to equalise but were unable to resist a Spanish side fresh from a 3-2 win over England at Wembley on Saturday.

Spain’s first home game since lifting the World Cup in July was preceded by Rodri parading the trophy on the pitch. The celebrations continued in Seville when Lamine, just as he did against England, opened the scoring in the second minute.

Alex Baena’s ball into the area was dummied by Fermin Lopez, and Lamine curled a first-time low shot inside the far post.

Baena then had an effort parried away by Croatia keeper Dominik Livakovic as Spain looked set to put the game out of reach early on, but the visitors drew level through Dion Beljo’s 28th-minute header.

Spain took less than three minutes to retake the lead. Lamine whipped a cross into the six-yard box from the right wing and Marc Pubill powered a header beyond Livakovic.

Lamine scored his second and Spain’s third in the 63rd minute, collecting Pedri’s pass in the box before drilling his shot into the net from a tight angle. Substitute Nico Williams wrapped up the win with an 89th-minute goal.

articles.title: Scotland 0-3 Switzerland: Jack Hendry sees red as Sebastien Pocognoli's side suffer Nations League defeat in head coach's first game at Hampden
articles.summary: Report as Scotland lose 3-0 to Switzerland in Nations League; Jack Hendry sent off inside 10 minutes in Sebastien Pocognoli's first home game in charge; Ricardo Rodriguez, Nico Elvedi and Zeki Amdouni on target for the Swiss; Pocognoli still searching for first win as Scotland head coach
articles.body:
Defender Jack Hendry was dismissed inside the first 10 minutes for denying a clear goalscoring opportunity when he hauled down Nottingham Forest's Dan Ndoye - before former AC Milan full-back Ricardo Rodriguez carefully curled the resulting free-kick into the top-left corner from the edge of the box.

This followed a period of confusion around the national stadium in which Serb referee Nenad Minakovic had originally awarded a penalty and shown Hendry a yellow card before his decision was corrected by VAR.

Scotland responded well and fought valiantly despite their numerical disadvantage but were eventually foiled early in the second half when Remo Freuler's low cross picked out Nico Elvedi who helped the ball into the far corner at the near post.

Burnley forward Zeki Amdouni then completed the scoring in the 82nd minute by stepping onto Ndoye's cutback and lashing the ball past Scotland stopper Angus Gunn.

The Scots travel to North Macedonia on Saturday then welcome Slovenia to Hampden next Tuesday - still in search of their first victory in Nations League B1.

9: PENALTY TO SWITZERLAND! Hendry brings down Ndoye and the referee points to the spot.

10: NO PENALTY! VAR has taken a look and the challenge was outside the box. But Hendry is sent off.

12: GOAL FOR SWITZERLAND! Well it was not a penalty but what a free-kick! Rodriguez steps up and blasts the ball past Gunn and the Swiss are ahead.

21: SCOTLAND WANT A PENALTY! John McGinn protests that he was being held as the corner is curled in, but it is play on. Andy Robertson then blasts the next corner over the bar.

29: BOOS AROUND HAMPDEN! Oli McBurnie is clipped as he looks to take the ball into the box. Free-kick? No says the referee.

45+1: YELLOW! Pocognoli picks up a booking as he shows his frustration at some of the refereeing decisions.

51: CHANCE! Ndoye sends the ball into the box, but Johan Manzambi cannot get to it in time and it goes past the post.

55: GOAL FOR SWITZERLAND! It is too easy for Switzerland. Elvedi sweeps home Ndoye's cross to double their advantage. Groans around Hampden.

82: GOAL FOR SWITZERLAND! It gets worse for Scotland. Amdouni gets on the end of Ndoye's cross and smashes the ball into the net. A tough night at Hampden Park.

'After eight minutes, game plan had to be put on the side'

Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli :

"Frustrating night, to be honest. Not a lot to say about the game, we can analyse the game with 80 per cent of the game with 10 men.

"Direct finish from the red card with a free-kick, so probably the worst situation that we can have.

"Should prefer maybe a penalty and to stay with with 11 men and to maybe show exactly what we what we planned for the game.

"But we start quite aggressive, front foot and after eight minutes the game plan has to put on the side and just see the team reacting well or not with 10 men.

"They did their best, to be honest. They had the great attitude to stick together, try to have the moment in transition or set pieces or something, but it never happened because Switzerland is a good side as well and they didn't give anything away."

Scotland captain Andy Robertson speaking to BBC Scotland:

"Your first home game under the new manager, you want to get off to a good start.

"It got off to the worst possible start getting a man sent off early doors. It was incredibly hard with 11 men on the pitch, it was even harder with 10.

"We hardly touched the ball second half, but it didn't stop the lads from fighting for each other.

"Football is about split second decisions, Jack Hendry has tried to nick the ball. As soon as the referee said it was outside the box I thought we would have been better taking the penalty and the yellow card.

"It's a difficult night but we won't try and let it get in the way of our process. We've got a new manager and a new squad so we have to try to stay positive.

"Going into the next game we have to try to forget about it.

"I think he [the manager] was proud of the fight that we showed. What we've planned for the last three days went completely out the window. We had to rip up the plan and try something else.

"Ultimately I don't think we'll take too much from this game in terms of how we want to look as a Scotland team.

"It's up to everyone to stay positive. I'm proud of how the camp has gone so far we just need to get the results."

articles.summary: El club italiano no permite que los dos argentinos acudan al adiós del 10 en Buenos Aires
articles.body: La Roma anunció este martes que los internacionales argentinos Paulo Dybala y Nahuel Molina, jugadores del conjunto italiano, "no participarán" en el partido entre la selección albiceleste y Benín del próximo 6 de octubre en Buenos Aires, que será la despedida de Lionel Messi del equipo nacional de su país. "La elección del club responde a razones deportivas y logísticas, relacionadas con la duración del viaje intercontinental y la proximidad de compromisos oficiales", explicó la entidad italiana en un comunicado entre los motivos para no autorizar su participación en ese encuentro. El Roma "reconoce el valor de la designación para ambos jugadores, vinculados a Lionel Messi y a los protagonistas con él de la victoria en el Mundial de 2022" y "desea expresar su más profundo respeto por Lionel Messi y su extraordinaria carrera, deseándole a él y a la Federación Argentina una velada especial". Messi se despedirá el próximo 6 de octubre de la selección argentina con el citado amistoso ante Benín en el estadio Monumental de Buenos Aires.

articles.summary: La opinión de José Vicente Hernáez
articles.body: Seguramente Gvardiol tendrá pesadillas unas cuantas noches con Lamine Yamal de protagonista. Gvardiol es un pedazo de defensa que del Dinamo de Zagreb se fue al Manchester City por un pastón descomunal para un jugador de sus características. Como digo (bueno, lo dicen todos los que lo conocen) es un defensa espectacular. Lamine Yamal no logró irse de él ni una sola vez y, sin embargo, Lamine Yamal fue la gran estrella de la noche en Sevilla. ¿Cómo se come eso? Muy sencillo. Cuando Lamine Yamal decidió aprovechar los espacios marcó dos goles (el segundo por donde parecía que el balón no podía entrar) y dio otro. Podría tomar nota un tal Vinícius. Ni todo el monte es orégano ni hay que obsesionarse con el regate. El resultado estaba cantado porque la selección española está muy por encima de cualquier otra a día de hoy. Sólo un accidente (un arbitraje perverso, por poner un ejemplo) podría frenar su sensacional trayectoria. Si no lo consiguió Inglaterra en Wembley, si no lo consiguieron los tres mosqueteros franceses en la reciente Copa del Mundo, menos aún lo iba a lograr Croacia en Sevilla. Y lo más grande es que los propios croatas lo sabían. Ni siquiera pudieron saborear el 1-1 logrado por el gigantón Beljo (ni Cubarsí ni Huijsen pudieron llegar a sus 1,95) porque un suspiro después Pubill se estrenaba como goleador. Luis de la Fuente hizo cinco cambios con respecto al equipo inicial de Wembley, lo cual quiere decir que en esta selección de cine (de cine y de autor) da igual quien juegue mientras no cambie el inquilino del banquillo. Oyarzábal, por ejemplo, no tuvo su noche, pero la selección hizo cuatro goles. Rodri no fue titular y aunque Zubimendi no es Rodri tampoco la selección dejó de jugar bien. En fin, que pase el siguiente

articles.title: Czech Republic 0-2 England: Anthony Gordon, Harry Kane net to give Three Lions first Nations League win
articles.summary: Match report as England recover from slow start to beat Czech Republic 2-0 in Prague to get Nations League campaign up and running, with second-half goals from Anthony Gordon and captain Harry Kane; Pavel Sulc sent off for hosts for first-half lunge on Elliot Anderson
articles.body:
While the Three Lions toiled in the early stages and nearly fell behind twice to presentable chances wasted by Sulc, Barcelona winger Gordon, supported by former Newcastle team-mate Lewis Hall, was a threat throughout. He came close to teeing up an opener while the two sides were still 11 vs 11, but saw Morgan Rogers curl his low cross against the far post on the turn.

Even once Sulc had been dismissed following a VAR review for a studs-up challenge on the shin of Elliot Anderson, it took a reshuffle from Thomas Tuchel and the half-time arrival of Eberechi Eze for many of his team-mates to catch up following a particularly nervous and passive opening period from the Three Lions.

But once they did, it was Gordon who took full advantage less than two minutes after the restart to stoop and turn Trent Alexander-Arnold's typically inviting cross home, netting for the third competitive game in a row.

Alexander-Arnold later revealed to ITV: "I spoke to Anthony at half-time and I said if I'm getting in the half spaces and putting them [crosses] in, make sure you get to the back post.

"You don't expect it to happen that quickly, but it did and it worked."

Hall, too, nearly got his just desserts when his dangerous low delivery was turned onto his own post by Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci with Rogers sniffing.

Coincidentally it would be a mix of Rogers and a deflection off Krejci that would tee-up Harry Kane, who else, to sweep home a second with England's next attack to put the result beyond doubt and add his 87th international goal.

That gave Tuchel the confidence to give out two competitive debuts to Alex Scott and Rio Ngumoha, both introduced shortly afterwards.

Scott would come within inches of a debut goal while Rogers and Eze would both go close to adding to England's lead, but they would at least see out a comfortable and much-needed win to get their Nations League campaign off the ground.

England head coach Thomas Tuchel on ITV:

"We played very professionally in the second half. We stepped up, we needed to be a bit more dynamic and put a bit more urgency into our play.

"We kept the intensity going and it was very professional. The effort was still there, it was a deserved victory. It's a bit strange to get an early red card, it's not the best for the spectators or the teams.

"But we got an important win, and that's what counts."

Gordon: I've been dying to play with Trent

England goalscorer and man-of-the-match Anthony Gordon on ITV:

"I make that run time and time again and only a certain type of player has got the technique, ability and bravery to make the mistake playing that pass.

"Credit to Trent, that's why he's so good. I've been dying to play with him for that reason.

"Trent's had his own journey with England. He would have liked to have played more than he has but he's a great character. He's a great addition."

articles.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold 'always believed' he would play for England again after first start in over two years
articles.summary: Trent Alexander-Arnold grabbed an assist on his first start for England in over two years; England recovered from slow start to beat Czech Republic 2-0 in Prague to get Nations League campaign up and running, with second-half goals from Anthony Gordon and captain Harry Kane
articles.body:
The 27-year-old defender made his first start for the Three Lions in almost two years in the 2-0 win over Czech Republic.

Alexander-Arnold had fallen out of favour under Tuchel over the past year or so, missing out on the World Cup squad this summer.

The Real Madrid player's last appearance for the national team came in June 2025, in a World Cup qualifier against Andorra.

But the former Liverpool defender made a good impression on his return, grabbing an assist for Anthony Gordon's opening goal as England swatted aside 10-man Czech Republic.

Alexander-Arnold told ITV Sport : "It was amazing, always an honour and pleasure to represent my country.

"It's been a long time but I've always believed that I can play for England and I always want to.

"The belief is always there, it's about proving it at club level. The manager gave me the chance tonight to play and to try to follow what he asked of me to the best of my ability. Hopefully he's happy with how I played."

On England's overall performance, he added: "I think it was good. They go down to 10 and there's more pressure on us to win, but it actually makes it more difficult. They get very compact and defend with a lot of players, we have a lot of the ball but it's hard to break them down.

"We got that early on in the second half which is what we needed. The longer that game goes on as a 0-0, it gets harder, they gain belief they can hold out and it was good to get that second goal."

Gordon was full of praise for Alexander-Arnold's assist that opened the scoring for England.

He said: "I make that run time and time again and only a certain type of player has got the technique, ability and bravery to make the mistake playing that pass. Credit to Trent, that's why he's so good. I've been dying to play with him for that reason.

"Trent's had his own journey with England. He would have liked to have played more than he has but he's a great character. He's a great addition."

Tuchel praises Alexander-Arnold performance

England head coach Thomas Tuchel speaking to ITV on the quality of Alexander-Arnold's assist:

"Yeah, not a lot could convert it! There was an awful lot for him to do, to guide it into the far post was an excellent finish. A good pass and a good goal.

"[Alexander-Arnold and Lewis Hall] were both good. The position in the second half suited Trent a little bit more than in the first half, and Lewis was excellent on the other side.

"We've used all outfield players in the first two games and credit to them."

articles.title: Josh Pate thinks AP Poll voters must be on drugs, and he’s not wrong
articles.summary: Another week of college football has come and gone, which means there’s another AP Poll for everybody to complain about. The weekend that was in college foot...
articles.body:
Another week of college football has come and gone, which means there's another AP Poll for everybody to complain about.

The weekend that was in college football produced some thrilling results that had fans on the edge of their seats waiting for the new AP Poll to come out on Sunday. No. 4 Ole Miss fell to No. 21 Florida. No. 20 Oregon spanked No. 12 USC. An exciting Mississippi State team that crept into the top-25 last week validated its entrance with a win over No. 19 Missouri. Not to mention top-ranked Texas slid by No. 14 Tennessee by a field goal.

There was bound to be a fair bit of shakeup in the AP Poll. But it appears as if, once again , voters were not up to the task, at least according to college football's voice of reason, Josh Pate.

Pate, who recently got his own weekly show on ESPN, took to his daily podcast on Monday to go after voters for what he views as some egregious misses in the most recent AP Top 25. Some of the voting was so bad in Pate's estimation that the only explanation is that the voters are on drugs.

"I think we need qualifiers to be an AP Poll voter," Pate began. "You're like, 'Josh, what kind of qualifier?' You need to have gone through the D.A.R.E. program," the college football commentator insisted, suggesting that AP voters must be in some drug-addled daze to put together the poll they did.

His first issue was with Florida's ranking. The Gators moved up from 21 to eight after beating the breaks off of top-five Ole Miss, but Pate thinks they didn't move up far enough.

"They would look, and they would say, 'Well, we bumped Florida up 13 spots.' That's not real logic! That's just something you say; that's bumper sticker logic. You're supposed to drive by, and I read that, and then it fades off in the distance, and I don't think through it critically, nor did you. You didn't bump Florida up anything. It's not real. It's just off feelings. It's not real anyway. That's not a reward. It's not like Jon Sumrall's standing in line [saying], 'Please.' There's a 13-spot bump. They went and disemboweled a top-five team last night. They went and ripped Ole Miss' spine out. They hung more yardage on them than Texas and Tennessee had combined. I don't care where they were last week. I don't care if they were unranked last week. Especially if you do this properly, early in the season there should be massive fluctuation in this thing."

Pate's next issue was with Missouri, a team that is still ranked after losing to Mississippi State.

"Missouri is still ranked. Why? Missouri was 19th based off feels last week. They're 25th based off drug use, essentially, because I don't know what on the resume constitutes being a top-25 team."

He then turns to Mississippi State, which moved up eight spots, but is still, according to Pate, hurt by its own brand.

"At this point, what would it take for Mississippi State to be a top-five team? They just beat Missouri. …Mississippi State just got a ranked win last night. They have three power-four wins. I am firmly convinced there are voters that still haven't watched them play. 'Oh, they got that quarterback, right?' That concludes our Mississippi State scouting report from an alarming number of AP voters. Drugs. Drugs! That's all you can say at this point."

On the opposite end of the brand spectrum is USC, a team that Pate is perplexed is "still 18th" after a home loss to Oregon.

"USC's on another level though. …Not only do they fail miserably, they fail miserably against Oregon's backup quarterback, and still get beat by double-digits at home. So it's like the annual pantsing of USC in a prime spot happens, and where do they fall? Outside the top-25? Outside of the top-30? No, they're 18th. Why are they still 18th? You know the answer. Drugs is the answer."

Pate was not alone. In fact, several other prominent football personalities agreed and brought additional receipts. ESPN's Kevin Clark dutifully noted that two AP voters simply forgot to rank Miami, currently the No. 4 team in the country, for the past three weeks. One of these voters ignored questions about his poll, and the other deleted his social media to avoid the backlash.

Responding to Clark, Yahoo Sports college football writer Dan Wolken advocated that polls like the AP's should be abolished altogether. "They don't serve a purpose anymore," he wrote.

In (slight) defense of the AP voters, keeping tabs on every single team in college football is no easy task, especially when many of these voters are beat reporters for one specific team. These voters are often in stadiums on Saturday covering their team, and can't keep tabs on several different games at once.

But that's exactly the point. Voters, who are ostensibly the most qualified people to make judgments on which teams are the best in the country, aren't even capable of putting together a coherent ranking. So what purpose does it serve other than giving fans and podcasters something to talk about?

Outside of some wholesale reform where the AP starts locking 50 people in a room for 12 hours every Saturday to watch every single college football game before submitting their ballots, this will continue to be a problem.

articles.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold: It is time for Thomas Tuchel to trust Real Madrid right-back
articles.summary: Having been overlooked for so long, Trent Alexander-Arnold produced a world-class moment on his return, writes Phil McNulty.
articles.body:
England head coach Thomas Tuchel's apparent lack of trust in Trent Alexander-Arnold has been one of the defining features - and a constant narrative - of his time in charge.

The 27-year-old right-back has won a Premier League title at Liverpool then moved to Real Madrid since he last started for England, selected as a left-back by interim manager Lee Carsley when scoring in a 3-1 Nations League win in Finland in October 2024.

He was ignored for England's World Cup squad last summer, despite right-back being a cursed role for Tuchel, making it appear that whatever questions the German had about that position, Alexander-Arnold was never going to be the answer.

So Tuchel's decision to recall Alexander-Arnold for this four-game Nations League camp came as a surprise, so emphatically had he been marginalised by England.

It was against this backdrop that Alexander-Arnold became the ninth right-back used by Tuchel in 24 games when he finally got his start against Czech Republic in Prague as England tried to recover from the 3-2 loss to World Cup holders Spain at Wembley.

And, with perhaps something to prove according to Tuchel, Alexander-Arnold did exactly that in one world-class moment that might convince his coach to train his sights on what he can do rather than what he cannot.

It is time, in other words, for Tuchel to offer Alexander-Arnold some trust.

Who continues to show how important they are? England player ratings

Kane and Gordon give England win over Czech Republic in Nations League

England, despite being in control, were toiling against the 10-man Czechs, who had seen danger man Pavel Sulc sent off after only 25 minutes for a reckless challenge on Elliot Anderson.

It was then, two minutes after the break, that Alexander-Arnold delivered a moment beyond those Tuchel has chosen ahead of him at right-back to pierce that stubborn resistance.

The player now officially known as "Trent", according to the name on the back of his shirt, had already made a 70-yard run into an attacking position in an attempt to increase England's attacking options.

When the move broke down, he regained possession before unfurling a magnificent right-foot delivery that floated in a teasing arc beyond three Czech defenders for Anthony Gordon to score with a stooping header that he made look far easier than it actually was.

Of course, Tuchel may still harbour those reservations about Alexander-Arnold's defending, and they were not put to the test here, but these few seconds showed exactly what he is about and what he can rightly argue is his unique selling point.

The defensive questions must wait for another day. The answers, whenever they come, would appear to shape Tuchel's thinking and Alexander-Arnold's England career, but he deserves the opportunity to provide them.

A delighted Tuchel told BBC Radio 5 Live: "He (Alexander-Arnold) did very well. He had an excellent assist. Overall, like everyone, he was professional, top attitude and one decisive action."

He added: "We never doubted that he can produce these kinds of assists. The deeper position in the second half suited him more than the higher position in the first half.

"Overall, I think we had a good and professional performance. Of course, the red card, especially an early red card, is such a heavy influence in the game. It makes the task sometimes a little bit more complicated psychologically."

'This must be close to make or break time'

Gordon, the grateful beneficiary of Alexander-Arnold's class, said: "I make that run time and time again and only a certain number of players have that ability, technique and bravery to be willing to make the mistake trying that pass. That's why he's so good and I've been dying to play with him for that reason.

"He's had his own journey with England. He would've liked to have played more than he has but he's been a great character during this camp. I've really enjoyed being around him."

Alexander-Arnold is a risk taker, both in the defensive and attacking context, but only Elliot Anderson (41) made more passes in the final third than he did (32), while only Anthony Gordon, with four, created more chances than the defender's three.

Tuchel, it should be stated, is not alone in having doubts about Alexander-Arnold.

Who can forget – although many would love to – Sir Gareth Southgate's ill-fated attempt to utilise Alexander-Arnold as a midfielder at Euro 2024? It was ditched after 54 minutes of England's second game against Denmark never to be seen again.

More will be revealed if Tuchel persists with Alexander-Arnold against Croatia behind closed doors in Rijeka on Saturday – but this must be close to make or break time for this lavishly-talented player who is 28 on 7 October.

If he cannot convince Tuchel in this camp, and surely that one moment of game-changing skill must be fixed in the head coach's mind, then you wonder if he ever will.

Alexander-Arnold said: "It was amazing. It's always an honour to represent my country. It's been a long time, but I've always believed I can play for England. That belief has always been there and it was about proving it at club level. The manager gave me a chance, now hopefully he is happy with how I played."

Alexander-Arnold, however, could not have done any more as England, who sealed the three points with captain Harry Kane's 87th goal in 123 international appearances, got their Nations League campaign going in Prague.

articles.title: ‘I will be very patient’ – Carlo Ancelotti defends Real Madrid star
articles.summary: Brazil national team head coach Carlo Ancelotti has on Tuesday moved to throw his full backing behind Real Madrid star Vinícius Jr.This comes amid what has b...
articles.body:
Brazil national team head coach Carlo Ancelotti has on Tuesday moved to throw his full backing behind Real Madrid star Vinícius Jr.

This comes amid what has been a difficult recent stretch for the 26-year-old on the pitch.

Vinícius has come in for heavy criticism over the early weeks of the new campaign, on the part of the Real Madrid faithful, the media, and neutrals alike.

Rewarded with a new big-money contract in Spain's capital over the summer, the gifted winger has since failed to showcase precisely why Florentino Pérez and co. were willing to commit to such a significant financial sacrifice.

Off the pace, lacking in one-on-one situations and wasteful in front of goal, Vinícius has found the net just once in eight appearances between La Liga and the Champions League.

Drawn on the name of his attacking star after Vinícius rounded out the scoring in Brazil's friendly victory over Australia on Tuesday, though, the aforementioned Carlo Ancelotti was quick to defend his former Real Madrid prodigy.

Adamant that Vinícius remains a central figure in his plans, Brazil's headmaster explained:

"Vini Jr deserves my patience. I know Vini very well. He's an important player for Brazil and he will continue to be in the future.

"Even when Vini isn't it in his best moment, he can still make the difference like he did today. Personally, I will be very patient, because he deserves this patience."

articles.title: Scotland 0-3 Switzerland: Sebastien Pocognoli hopes to remember Hampden bow fondly despite defeat
articles.summary: Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli hopes "we will remember this night differently later on" as his Hampden bow ends with a 3-0 defeat by Switzerland.
articles.body:
Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli hopes to "remember this night differently later on" after his Hampden debut ended in a deflating Nations League defeat by Switzerland.

Off the back of a goalless draw in Ljubljana on Saturday in his first game as Scotland boss, Pocognoli's side slumped to a 3-0 loss in Glasgow's southside on Tuesday.

Scotland are now without a clean sheet in eight home matches and, perhaps more worryingly, have failed to score in six of their nine games this year.

Pocognoli promised a more attacking approach, built on a high press and high energy, but those ideals were undermined by Jack Hendry's 11th-minute red card.

Ricardo Rodriguez rifled the subsequent free-kick past Angus Gunn and the Swiss never ceded control, with Leeds United centre-back Nico Elvedi and Burnley midfielder Zeki Amdouni adding to the scoreline in the second half.

The Scots are third in their Nations League group after two games, with a trip to bottom side North Macedonia on Saturday before the visit of Slovenia on Tuesday.

"It's not easy against a good team to be with 10 men," said Pocognoli, who was appointed as Steve Clarke's successor in August.

"It will be more about the reaction. We had an unlucky red card, punished with the free-kick, that's the worst scenario. The guys did the best they could and hopefully we will remember this night differently later on.

"We have to move on and get a good result in North Macedonia."

articles.title: Kick It Out receives record 1,744 discrimination reports in first year of Football United strategy
articles.summary: Kick It Out's Year One Impact Report was published on Tuesday as the organisation attempts to make football more inclusive and representative; Kick It Out says the increase in reports should not be viewed solely as a deterioration in football's culture
articles.body:
The organisation says a rise in anti-immigrant language contributed to the increase, while improved reporting relationships with groups including Her Game Too, The Frank Soo Foundation and Football v Homophobia also gave more people confidence to report incidents.

More than 100 reports were received through those new channels during the 2025/26 season.

Kick It Out says the increase in reports should not be viewed solely as a deterioration in football's culture, pointing to greater confidence among communities to report discrimination and improved relationships with partner organisations.

The number of reporting partnerships is expected to increase during the 2026/27 season.

Samuel Okafor, Kick It Out's chief executive, said: "At a time of rising discrimination and where we need action to make the game more inclusive and representative of all communities, football must be more united to take on its challenges.

"Although our Impact Report shows a year of progress working alongside existing and new partners, we know that with further collaboration we can build on our policy, campaigning, education and reporting programmes to make the game more welcoming for everyone."

Kick It Out's Year One Impact Report, published on Tuesday, highlights the scale of the challenge facing football as the organisation attempts to make the game more inclusive and representative.

The report covers the first year of Football United, a five-year strategy launched in September 2025 with four key goals: everyone is included; everyone is represented on the pitch; everyone can lead off the pitch; and everyone stands up to discrimination.

The organisation also highlighted several other developments during the first year of its strategy.

More than 11,000 people accessed Kick It Out education programmes, while 583 people attended its Raise Your Game development programme and 148 took part in Fan Education.

A partnership with Guinness 0.0 saw Kick It Out take its work into pubs, with more than 3,000 Greene King staff receiving education on how to recognise and respond to discrimination.

The start of the 2025/26 season also saw professional clubs publish workforce diversity data for the first time under FA Rule N, providing greater visibility of representation in leadership positions across the game.

Kick It Out says it worked with more than 20 organisations to submit proposals to the Independent Football Regulator, contributing to increased board-level accountability on equality, diversity and inclusion, as well as representation targets for club boards and senior leadership positions.

The organisation also worked with partners on issues including online abuse, sexism and misogyny, faith-based discrimination and inclusion for underrepresented communities.

Okafor added: "This is only year one of the strategy, so we know there is so much more to achieve, but we have ambitious plans for the coming season where we will expand grassroots anti-discrimination education, increase Fan Education delivery with support from the Premier League and grow Raise Your Game.

"We are determined to keep building a game where everyone is included, and everyone is united in tackling discrimination wherever it happens."
